Entries.Name: Domain servers
Entries.Description: Enabled computer accounts with a server OS.
Entries.WhereToRun: Any domain-joined computer with RSAT.
Entries.Code:
function Get-ADServerList {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Discovers the servers in the domain (enabled computer accounts with a server OS).
.DESCRIPTION
Copy the Name column into "Run on these computers" to run any library entry across them.
.PARAMETER SearchBase
Only computers under this OU.
.PARAMETER Server
Domain or DC to ask.
.PARAMETER ActiveDays
Only computers that logged on within this many days (0 = all).
.EXAMPLE
Get-ADServerList -ActiveDays 30
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [string]$SearchBase,
        [string]$Server,
        [int]$ActiveDays = 30
    )
    $p = @{ Filter = "OperatingSystem -like '*Server*' -and Enabled -eq `$true"; Properties = 'OperatingSystem', 'LastLogonDate', 'IPv4Address', 'DNSHostName' }
    if ($SearchBase) { $p.SearchBase = $SearchBase }
    if ($Server) { $p.Server = $Server }
    $cut = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$ActiveDays)
    Get-ADComputer @p |
        Where-Object { $ActiveDays -le 0 -or $_.LastLogonDate -ge $cut } |
        Sort-Object Name |
        Select-Object Name, DNSHostName, IPv4Address, OperatingSystem, LastLogonDate
}
Entries.Notes:
Discovers the servers in the domain (enabled computer accounts with a server OS).
Copy the Name column into "Run on these computers" to run any library entry across them.

Entries.Name: Empty groups
Entries.WhereToRun: Any domain-joined computer with RSAT.
Entries.Code:
function Find-EmptyADGroup {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Groups that have no members - the quick wins in a group cleanup (built-in groups excluded).
.PARAMETER SearchBase
Only groups under this OU.
.PARAMETER Server
Domain or DC.
.EXAMPLE
Find-EmptyADGroup -SearchBase 'OU=Groups,DC=contoso,DC=com'
.NOTES
Empty is not the same as unused: a group can still be referenced by ACLs or GPOs (Find-FolderAclEntry, Find-GpoText).
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$SearchBase, [string]$Server)
    $p = @{ Filter = '*'; Properties = 'Members', 'whenCreated', 'whenChanged', 'Description', 'isCriticalSystemObject' }
    if ($SearchBase) { $p.SearchBase = $SearchBase }
    if ($Server) { $p.Server = $Server }
    Get-ADGroup @p | Where-Object { @($_.Members).Count -eq 0 -and -not $_.isCriticalSystemObject -and $_.DistinguishedName -notmatch 'CN=Builtin,' } |
        Sort-Object whenChanged |
        Select-Object Name, GroupScope, GroupCategory, whenCreated, whenChanged, Description, @{ N = 'OU'; E = { $_.DistinguishedName -replace '^CN=[^,]+,', '' } }
}
Entries.Notes:
Groups that have no members - the quick wins in a group cleanup (built-in groups excluded).

Empty is not the same as unused: a group can still be referenced by ACLs or GPOs (Find-FolderAclEntry, Find-GpoText).

Entries.Name: gMSA check
Entries.Description: Is a gMSA usable here: KDS key, allowed hosts, test.
Entries.WhereToRun: The server that will use the gMSA (with RSAT ActiveDirectory).
Entries.Code:
function Test-GmsaReady {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Checks a group Managed Service Account can be used on this computer.
.DESCRIPTION
Shows whether a KDS root key exists, which principals may retrieve the account's password,
and the result of Test-ADServiceAccount on this computer.
.PARAMETER Name
The gMSA name, without the trailing $.
.EXAMPLE
Test-GmsaReady -Name svc-PwdNotify
.NOTES
Run on the server that will use the gMSA. Install-ADServiceAccount must have been run there.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Name)
    $kds = @(Get-KdsRootKey -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    $acct = Get-ADServiceAccount -Identity $Name -Properties PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword, DNSHostName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $test = $false
    try { $test = Test-ADServiceAccount -Identity $Name -ErrorAction Stop } catch { Write-Warning $_.Exception.Message }
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Account          = $Name
        Exists           = [bool]$acct
        KdsRootKeys      = $kds.Count
        KdsEffective     = $(if ($kds.Count) { ($kds | Sort-Object EffectiveTime | Select-Object -First 1).EffectiveTime } else { $null })
        AllowedToRetrieve = $(if ($acct) { ($acct.PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split ',')[0] -replace '^CN=' }) -join ', ' } else { '' })
        UsableHere       = $test
        Computer         = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
Checks a group Managed Service Account can be used on this computer.
Shows whether a KDS root key exists, which principals may retrieve the account's password,
and the result of Test-ADServiceAccount on this computer.

Run on the server that will use the gMSA. Install-ADServiceAccount must have been run there.

Entries.Name: gMSA create
Entries.Description: Creates KDS key, host group and gMSA in one go.
Entries.WhereToRun: A computer with RSAT ActiveDirectory, as a Domain Admin.
Entries.Notes:
Creates a group Managed Service Account and the group of servers allowed to use it, creating the KDS root key first if the domain has none.
Steps: check Get-KdsRootKey (add one with -EffectiveImmediately if missing - in a multi-DC domain wait up to 10 hours
for replication, or use a backdated key in a lab only); create the host group; add the servers' computer accounts;
create the gMSA allowed to retrieve its password by that group.

Each server must reboot (or run klist -li 0x3e7 purge) before it sees its new group membership. Then run Install-GmsaOnServer on it.

function Get-GroupMemberDomain {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Members of a group, with the domain each member comes from (shows members across a trust).
.PARAMETER Identity
The group name.
.PARAMETER Server
Domain or DC that holds the group.
.PARAMETER Recursive
Expand nested groups.
.EXAMPLE
Get-GroupMemberDomain -Identity 'Server Admins' -Server domain1.com -Recursive
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Identity,
        [string]$Server,
        [switch]$Recursive
    )
    $p = @{ Identity = $Identity; Recursive = [bool]$Recursive }
    if ($Server) { $p.Server = $Server }
    Get-ADGroupMember @p | ForEach-Object {
        $dcs = @(([regex]::Matches($_.distinguishedName, 'DC=([^,]+)')) | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value })
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Name           = $_.Name
            SamAccountName = $_.SamAccountName
            Type           = $_.objectClass
            SourceDomain   = ($dcs -join '.')
            ForeignSID     = ($_.distinguishedName -match 'ForeignSecurityPrincipals')
        }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Members of a group, with the domain each member comes from (shows members across a trust).

function Get-CrossDomainGroup {
<#
.SYNOPSIS

Domains to query, one per line.

Entries.Name: LDAP bind test
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer that will connect (e.g. the Ignition gateway).
Entries.Code:
function Test-LdapBind {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Binds to a DC with a username and password (plain LDAP or LDAPS) and runs a small search - proves the credentials, port and base DN an application is configured with.
.PARAMETER Server
DC host name. For LDAPS use the name on the DC certificate.
.PARAMETER Credential
The bind account the application uses.
.PARAMETER UseSsl
LDAPS on 636 (otherwise 389).
.PARAMETER SearchBase
Base DN the app searches, e.g. OU=Users,DC=contoso,DC=com. Empty = the domain root.
.PARAMETER Filter
LDAP filter to count.
.EXAMPLE
Test-LdapBind -Server dc1.contoso.com -UseSsl -SearchBase 'OU=Users,DC=contoso,DC=com'
.NOTES
A bind that works here but fails in a Java app over LDAPS is usually certificate trust (Test-ServerCertificate, Import-JavaTrustedCertificate).
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Server, [Parameter(Mandatory)] [pscredential]$Credential, [switch]$UseSsl, [string]$SearchBase, [string]$Filter = '(objectClass=user)')
    Add-Type -AssemblyName System.DirectoryServices.Protocols
    $port = if ($UseSsl) { 636 } else { 389 }
    $id = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapDirectoryIdentifier($Server, $port)
    $c = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection($id, $Credential.GetNetworkCredential(), [System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.AuthType]::Negotiate)
    $c.SessionOptions.ProtocolVersion = 3
    if ($UseSsl) { $c.SessionOptions.SecureSocketLayer = $true }
    $c.Timeout = [TimeSpan]::FromSeconds(15)
    $sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    try {
        $c.Bind()
        $bindMs = $sw.ElapsedMilliseconds
        if (-not $SearchBase) {
            $root = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.SearchRequest('', '(objectClass=*)', [System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.SearchScope]::Base, 'defaultNamingContext')
            $SearchBase = [string]($c.SendRequest($root).Entries[0].Attributes['defaultNamingContext'][0])
        }
        $req = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.SearchRequest($SearchBase, $Filter, [System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.SearchScope]::Subtree, 'sAMAccountName')
        $req.SizeLimit = 1000
        $count = 0
        try { $count = $c.SendRequest($req).Entries.Count } catch [System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.DirectoryOperationException] { $count = "1000+ ($($_.Exception.Message))" }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Server = $Server; Port = $port; Bind = 'OK'; BindMs = $bindMs; User = $Credential.UserName; SearchBase = $SearchBase; Matches = $count }
    }
    catch { [pscustomobject]@{ Server = $Server; Port = $port; Bind = 'FAILED'; BindMs = $sw.ElapsedMilliseconds; User = $Credential.UserName; SearchBase = $SearchBase; Matches = $_.Exception.Message } }
    finally { $c.Dispose() }
}
Entries.Notes:
Binds to a DC with a username and password (plain LDAP or LDAPS) and runs a small search - proves the credentials, port and base DN an application is configured with.

A bind that works here but fails in a Java app over LDAPS is usually certificate trust (Test-ServerCertificate, Import-JavaTrustedCertificate).

Entries.Code:
function Get-LockoutStatus {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
How many more bad passwords a user (or every user) can enter before the account locks.
.DESCRIPTION
Compares each account's BadLogonCount with the domain lockout threshold. BadLogonCount is
kept per domain controller and not replicated, so by default the PDC emulator is asked (it
sees every bad attempt). The count resets after the lockout observation window, so 0 can
follow recent failures.
.PARAMETER Username
sAMAccountName to check. Leave empty to list every user.
.PARAMETER WarnWithin
Only list users this many attempts (or fewer) from lockout. 0 = list all.
.PARAMETER Server
Domain controller to ask. Empty = the PDC emulator of the current domain.
.EXAMPLE
Get-LockoutStatus -Username jsmith
.EXAMPLE
Get-LockoutStatus -WarnWithin 2
.NOTES
If the domain uses fine-grained password policies (PSOs), a user's threshold can differ
from the default domain policy; the PSO threshold is used when one applies.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [string]$Username,
        [int]$WarnWithin = 0,
        [string]$Server
    )
    if (-not $Server) { $Server = (Get-ADDomain).PDCEmulator }
    $policy = Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Server $Server
    $props = 'BadLogonCount', 'LockedOut', 'LastBadPasswordAttempt', 'DisplayName', 'msDS-ResultantPSO'
    $users = if ($Username) { Get-ADUser -Identity $Username -Server $Server -Properties $props }
             else { Get-ADUser -Filter * -Server $Server -Properties $props }
    $psoCache = @{}
    foreach ($u in $users) {
        $threshold = $policy.LockoutThreshold
        $pso = $u.'msDS-ResultantPSO'
        if ($pso) {
            if (-not $psoCache.ContainsKey($pso)) { $psoCache[$pso] = (Get-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Identity $pso -Server $Server).LockoutThreshold }
            $threshold = $psoCache[$pso]
        }
        $remaining = if ($threshold -gt 0) { $threshold - [int]$u.BadLogonCount } else { $null }
        if ($WarnWithin -gt 0 -and ($null -eq $remaining -or $remaining -gt $WarnWithin)) { continue }
        [pscustomobject]@{
            User              = $u.SamAccountName
            DisplayName       = $u.DisplayName
            LockedOut         = $u.LockedOut
            BadAttempts       = [int]$u.BadLogonCount
            Threshold         = $(if ($threshold -gt 0) { $threshold } else { 'none' })
            AttemptsRemaining = $remaining
            LastBadAttempt    = $u.LastBadPasswordAttempt
            Policy            = $(if ($pso) { 'PSO' } else { 'Default domain policy' })
        }
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
How many more bad passwords a user (or every user) can enter before the account locks.
Compares each account's BadLogonCount with the domain lockout threshold. BadLogonCount is
kept per domain controller and not replicated, so by default the PDC emulator is asked (it
sees every bad attempt). The count resets after the lockout observation window, so 0 can
follow recent failures.

If the domain uses fine-grained password policies (PSOs), a user's threshold can differ
from the default domain policy; the PSO threshold is used when one applies.

function Find-CertificateAuthority {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
The enterprise certificate authorities published in Active Directory (name, server, CA certificate) - where certsrv lives.
.EXAMPLE
Find-CertificateAuthority
.NOTES
Web enrollment, if installed, is http://<server>/certsrv. The CA console is certsrv.msc on that server.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    $root = [ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE'
    $cfg = [string]$root.configurationNamingContext
    $base = [ADSI]("LDAP://CN=Enrollment Services,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,$cfg")
    foreach ($ca in $base.Children) {
        $cert = $null
        try { $cert = New-Object System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2(, [byte[]]$ca.cACertificate[0]) } catch { }
        [pscustomobject]@{
            CAName      = [string]$ca.cn
            Server      = [string]$ca.dNSHostName
            Config      = "$($ca.dNSHostName)\$($ca.cn)"
            CertSubject = $(if ($cert) { $cert.Subject } else { '' })
            CertExpires = $(if ($cert) { $cert.NotAfter } else { $null })
            Thumbprint  = $(if ($cert) { $cert.Thumbprint } else { '' })
            WebEnroll   = "http://$($ca.dNSHostName)/certsrv"
        }
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
The enterprise certificate authorities published in Active Directory (name, server, CA certificate) - where certsrv lives.

Web enrollment, if installed, is http://<server>/certsrv. The CA console is certsrv.msc on that server.

function Export-CertificateBase64 {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Exports a certificate from a Windows store as a Base-64 (PEM-style) .cer file - the format keytool and Java want.
.PARAMETER Subject
Text in the subject (e.g. your CA name) - or use -Thumbprint.
.PARAMETER Thumbprint
Exact certificate thumbprint.
.PARAMETER Store
Store to look in. Root CAs: Cert:\LocalMachine\Root. Intermediates: Cert:\LocalMachine\CA.
.PARAMETER OutFile
Where to write the .cer file.
.EXAMPLE
Export-CertificateBase64 -Subject 'contoso-ROOT-CA' -Store Cert:\LocalMachine\Root -OutFile C:\Temp\contoso-root-ca.cer
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [string]$Subject,
        [string]$Thumbprint,
        [string]$Store = 'Cert:\LocalMachine\Root',
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$OutFile
    )
    $certs = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $Store | Where-Object { ($Thumbprint -and $_.Thumbprint -eq $Thumbprint) -or ($Subject -and $_.Subject -like "*$Subject*") })
    if ($certs.Count -eq 0) { throw "No certificate in $Store matches." }
    if ($certs.Count -gt 1) { Write-Warning "$($certs.Count) certificates match - exporting the newest. Use -Thumbprint to pick one."; $certs = @($certs | Sort-Object NotAfter -Descending | Select-Object -First 1) }
    $c = $certs[0]
    if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($c.Subject, "Export to $OutFile")) {
        $b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String($c.RawData, [System.Base64FormattingOptions]::InsertLineBreaks)
        $text = "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`r`n$b64`r`n-----END CERTIFICATE-----`r`n"
        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($OutFile, $text, (New-Object System.Text.ASCIIEncoding))
        [pscustomobject]@{ File = $OutFile; Subject = $c.Subject; NotAfter = $c.NotAfter; Thumbprint = $c.Thumbprint }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Exports a certificate from a Windows store as a Base-64 (PEM-style) .cer file - the format keytool and Java want.

function Test-CertificateFile {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Runs "certutil -verify -urlfetch" on a certificate file: chain building, expiry and revocation (CRL/OCSP) as this computer sees it.
.PARAMETER Path
The certificate file (.cer or .crt).
.EXAMPLE
Test-CertificateFile -Path C:\Temp\contoso-root-ca.cer
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path)
    $out = @(certutil -verify -urlfetch $Path 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ })
    $summary = $out | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Leaf certificate revocation|Verified|dwErrorStatus|ERROR|CERT_TRUST|Cannot find|expired|revoked' } | Select-Object -First 15
    [pscustomobject]@{ File = $Path; ExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE; Summary = ($summary -join ' | '); FullOutput = ($out -join "`n") }
}

Entries.Code:
function Get-ExpiringCertificate {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Certificates in the computer (and current user) stores that are expired or expire within N days.
.PARAMETER Days
Expiring within this many days. Expired ones are always listed.
.PARAMETER Store
Stores to check, e.g. Cert:\LocalMachine\My, Cert:\LocalMachine\WebHosting.
.PARAMETER IncludeAll
List every certificate, not just expiring ones.
.EXAMPLE
Get-ExpiringCertificate -Days 60
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [int]$Days = 30,
        [string[]]$Store = @('Cert:\LocalMachine\My', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\WebHosting', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\Remote Desktop', 'Cert:\CurrentUser\My'),
        [switch]$IncludeAll
    )
    $now = Get-Date
    foreach ($s in $Store) {
        foreach ($c in @(Get-ChildItem -Path $s -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_ -is [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2] })) {
            $left = [math]::Floor(($c.NotAfter - $now).TotalDays)
            if (-not $IncludeAll -and $left -gt $Days) { continue }
            [pscustomobject]@{
                Computer   = $env:COMPUTERNAME
                Store      = $s
                Subject    = $c.Subject
                Issuer     = $c.Issuer
                NotAfter   = $c.NotAfter
                DaysLeft   = $left
                Status     = $(if ($left -lt 0) { 'EXPIRED' } elseif ($left -le $Days) { 'Expiring' } else { 'OK' })
                Thumbprint = $c.Thumbprint
                DnsNames   = ((@($c.DnsNameList) | ForEach-Object { $_.Unicode }) -join ', ')
                PrivateKey = $c.HasPrivateKey
            }
        }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Certificates in the computer (and current user) stores that are expired or expire within N days.

function Test-InstallerSignature {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Verifies a downloaded installer: Authenticode signature (who signed it, is it valid) and its hash, optionally compared with the published one.
.PARAMETER Path
The file (msi, exe ...).
.PARAMETER ExpectedHash
The vendor's published hash (SHA256 or SHA512), to compare.
.PARAMETER Algorithm
Hash algorithm.
.EXAMPLE
Test-InstallerSignature -Path 'C:\Temp\Firefox Setup 140.17.0esr.msi' -Algorithm SHA512 -ExpectedHash <hash from SHA512SUMS>
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path, [string]$ExpectedHash, [ValidateSet('SHA256', 'SHA512', 'SHA1')] [string]$Algorithm = 'SHA256')
    $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath $Path
    $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $Path -Algorithm $Algorithm).Hash
    [pscustomobject]@{
        File        = Split-Path -Path $Path -Leaf
        Signature   = [string]$sig.Status
        SignedBy    = $(if ($sig.SignerCertificate) { $sig.SignerCertificate.Subject } else { '' })
        SignerValid = $(if ($sig.SignerCertificate) { $sig.SignerCertificate.NotAfter } else { $null })
        Timestamped = [bool]$sig.TimeStamperCertificate
        Algorithm   = $Algorithm
        Hash        = $hash
        HashMatches = $(if ($ExpectedHash) { $hash -ieq $ExpectedHash.Trim() } else { $null })
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Verifies a downloaded installer: Authenticode signature (who signed it, is it valid) and its hash, optionally compared with the published one.

Entries.Name: Java keystore import
Entries.Description: Adds a CA to cacerts; fixes PKIX errors.
Entries.WhereToRun: The server running the Java application, elevated. Restart the application afterwards.
Entries.Code:
function Import-JavaTrustedCertificate {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Adds a CA certificate to a Java truststore (cacerts) so Java trusts servers it issued - the fix for "PKIX path building failed".
.DESCRIPTION
Java applications with a bundled JRE (Ignition, FactoryTalk, ...) get a fresh cacerts with each
upgrade, losing CA certificates imported before. Export your root (and intermediate) CA as Base-64
(.cer), import it here, then restart the application service. A backup of cacerts is made first.
.PARAMETER CertificateFile
The CA certificate (.cer, Base-64 or DER).
.PARAMETER Alias
Name for it in the truststore, e.g. contoso-root-ca.
.PARAMETER Keystore
The cacerts file. Empty = Ignition's bundled JRE (lib\runtime\jre-win\lib\security\cacerts).
.PARAMETER KeytoolPath
keytool.exe. Empty = next to the keystore's JRE.
.PARAMETER StorePassword
Truststore password (Java default "changeit").
.EXAMPLE
Import-JavaTrustedCertificate -CertificateFile C:\Temp\contoso-root-ca.cer -Alias contoso-root-ca -StorePassword <secure>
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$CertificateFile,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Alias,
        [string]$Keystore,
        [string]$KeytoolPath,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [securestring]$StorePassword
    )
    if (-not $Keystore) {
        $Keystore = @(Get-ChildItem 'C:\Program Files\Inductive Automation\Ignition\lib\runtime' -Recurse -Filter cacerts -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName }) | Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $Keystore) { throw 'No cacerts found under the Ignition runtime. Give -Keystore.' }
    }
    if (-not $KeytoolPath) {
        $jreRoot = Split-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $Keystore -Parent) -Parent) -Parent
        $KeytoolPath = Join-Path $jreRoot 'bin\keytool.exe'
    }
    if (-not (Test-Path $KeytoolPath)) { throw "keytool.exe not found at $KeytoolPath. Give -KeytoolPath." }
    $pw = (New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential('x', $StorePassword)).GetNetworkCredential().Password
    if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($Keystore, "Import $CertificateFile as '$Alias'")) { return }
    $bak = "$Keystore.bak-$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd-HHmmss)"
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $Keystore -Destination $bak -ErrorAction Stop
    $out = @(& $KeytoolPath -importcert -noprompt -trustcacerts -alias $Alias -file $CertificateFile -keystore $Keystore -storepass $pw 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ })
    $ok = ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)
    [pscustomobject]@{ Keystore = $Keystore; Alias = $Alias; Imported = $ok; Backup = $bak; Output = ($out -join ' '); Next = 'Restart the application service so Java re-reads cacerts.' }
}
Entries.Notes:
Adds a CA certificate to a Java truststore (cacerts) so Java trusts servers it issued - the fix for "PKIX path building failed".
Java applications with a bundled JRE (Ignition, FactoryTalk, ...) get a fresh cacerts with each
upgrade, losing CA certificates imported before. Export your root (and intermediate) CA as Base-64
(.cer), import it here, then restart the application service. A backup of cacerts is made first.

Entries.Name: TLS cert check
Entries.Description: Cert a server presents (LDAPS, HTTPS) + trust.
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer that has to trust the server (e.g. the application server).
Entries.Code:
function Test-ServerCertificate {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Connects to a TLS port (LDAPS 636 by default) and shows the certificate the server presents, its chain, dates, and whether this computer trusts it.
.DESCRIPTION
"PKIX path building failed" in a Java application (Ignition, etc.) means Java's own truststore does not
trust the issuing CA - even if Windows does. This shows which CA issued the certificate so you can
export that CA and import it into the Java truststore.
.PARAMETER ComputerName
Server name, e.g. a domain controller.
.PARAMETER Port
636 LDAPS, 3269 GC over SSL, 443 HTTPS ...
.EXAMPLE
Test-ServerCertificate -ComputerName inmdc01.contoso.com -Port 636
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$ComputerName, [int]$Port = 636)
    $state = @{ Errors = 'None'; Chain = @() }
    $tcp = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient
    try {
        $iar = $tcp.BeginConnect($ComputerName, $Port, $null, $null)
        if (-not $iar.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne(5000)) { throw "Could not connect to ${ComputerName}:$Port within 5 seconds." }
        $tcp.EndConnect($iar)
        $cb = [System.Net.Security.RemoteCertificateValidationCallback] {
            param($sender, $cert, $chain, $errors)
            $state.Errors = [string]$errors
            $state.Chain = @($chain.ChainElements | ForEach-Object { $_.Certificate.Subject })
            return $true
        }
        $ssl = New-Object System.Net.Security.SslStream($tcp.GetStream(), $false, $cb)
        $ssl.AuthenticateAsClient($ComputerName)
        $c = New-Object System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2($ssl.RemoteCertificate)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Server       = "${ComputerName}:$Port"
            Subject      = $c.Subject
            Issuer       = $c.Issuer
            NotAfter     = $c.NotAfter
            DaysLeft     = [math]::Floor(($c.NotAfter - (Get-Date)).TotalDays)
            TrustedHere  = ($state.Errors -eq 'None')
            Problems     = $state.Errors
            Chain        = ($state.Chain -join '  <-  ')
            Protocol     = [string]$ssl.SslProtocol
            Thumbprint   = $c.Thumbprint
        }
        $ssl.Dispose()
    }
    finally { $tcp.Close() }
}
Entries.Notes:
Connects to a TLS port (LDAPS 636 by default) and shows the certificate the server presents, its chain, dates, and whether this computer trusts it.
"PKIX path building failed" in a Java application (Ignition, etc.) means Java's own truststore does not
trust the issuing CA - even if Windows does. This shows which CA issued the certificate so you can
export that CA and import it into the Java truststore.

Entries.Name: Trusted roots
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer whose trust you are checking.

function Get-TrustedRootCert {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Certificates in the Trusted Root and Intermediate stores whose subject matches a name, with expiry and thumbprint.
.PARAMETER Subject
Text in the subject, e.g. the CA name. Empty = all.
.PARAMETER IncludeIntermediate
Also the Intermediate CA store.
.EXAMPLE
Get-TrustedRootCert -Subject Contoso
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Subject, [switch]$IncludeIntermediate)
    $stores = @('Cert:\LocalMachine\Root')
    if ($IncludeIntermediate) { $stores += 'Cert:\LocalMachine\CA' }
    foreach ($s in $stores) {
        Get-ChildItem $s | Where-Object { -not $Subject -or $_.Subject -like "*$Subject*" } |
            Sort-Object Subject |
            Select-Object @{ N = 'Store'; E = { ($s -split '\\')[-1] } }, Subject, NotAfter, @{ N = 'DaysLeft'; E = { [math]::Floor(($_.NotAfter - (Get-Date)).TotalDays) } }, Thumbprint
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Certificates in the Trusted Root and Intermediate stores whose subject matches a name, with expiry and thumbprint.

function Get-FolderSize {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Size of a folder and of each of its subfolders, largest first.

Only the largest N subfolders.

Get-FolderSize -Path C:\Windows\Temp -Top 10

    [CmdletBinding()]

Entries.Name: IPv6 fallback check
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer with slow connections or logons.
Entries.Code:
function Test-IPv6Fallback {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Whether a host has IPv6 (AAAA) records and whether IPv6 actually connects - an unreachable AAAA makes Windows wait before falling back to IPv4.
.PARAMETER ComputerName
Hosts to test, one per line.
.PARAMETER Port
Port to try on each address.
.EXAMPLE
Test-IPv6Fallback -ComputerName dc1.domain2.ads -Port 389
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string[]]$ComputerName, [int]$Port = 389)
    foreach ($c in $ComputerName) {
        $v4 = @(Resolve-DnsName $c -Type A -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object IPAddress | ForEach-Object { $_.IPAddress })
        $v6 = @(Resolve-DnsName $c -Type AAAA -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object IPAddress | ForEach-Object { $_.IPAddress })
        $test = {
            param($addr)
            $t = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient($(if ($addr -match ':') { [System.Net.Sockets.AddressFamily]::InterNetworkV6 } else { [System.Net.Sockets.AddressFamily]::InterNetwork }))
            $sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
            $ok = $false
            try { $iar = $t.BeginConnect($addr, $Port, $null, $null); $ok = $iar.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne(3000) -and $t.Connected } catch { } finally { $t.Close() }
            "$addr=$(if ($ok) { "ok $($sw.ElapsedMilliseconds)ms" } else { 'FAILED' })"
        }
        $r4 = @($v4 | ForEach-Object { & $test $_ }) -join ', '
        $r6 = @($v6 | ForEach-Object { & $test $_ }) -join ', '
        [pscustomobject]@{ Host = $c; IPv4 = $r4; IPv6 = $(if ($v6.Count) { $r6 } else { '(no AAAA)' }); Problem = ($v6.Count -gt 0 -and $r6 -notmatch 'ok') }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Whether a host has IPv6 (AAAA) records and whether IPv6 actually connects - an unreachable AAAA makes Windows wait before falling back to IPv4.

Entries.Name: DC locator test
Entries.Description: Which DC the locator picks, and how fast.
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer with slow logons (e.g. the terminal server).
Entries.Code:
function Test-DcLocator {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Asks DC Locator for a DC in a domain several times (forced, uncached) and reports which DCs it picked and how long each answer took.
.PARAMETER Domain
Domain to locate a DC in.
.PARAMETER Samples
How many tries.
.PARAMETER GlobalCatalog
Ask for a global catalog.
.EXAMPLE
Test-DcLocator -Domain domain2.ads -Samples 10 -GlobalCatalog
.NOTES
If one DC shows up and it is slow or unhealthy (Get-DcHealthReport), that is the one logons hang on.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Domain, [int]$Samples = 5, [switch]$GlobalCatalog)
    for ($i = 1; $i -le $Samples; $i++) {
        $a = @("/dsgetdc:$Domain", '/force')
        if ($GlobalCatalog) { $a += '/gc' }
        $sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
        $raw = @(nltest @a 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ })
        $ms = $sw.ElapsedMilliseconds
        $dc = ($raw | Where-Object { $_ -match 'DC:\s*\\\\(\S+)' } | Select-Object -First 1)
        $addr = ($raw | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Address:\s*\\\\(\S+)' } | Select-Object -First 1)
        $site = ($raw | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Dc Site Name:\s*(\S+)' } | Select-Object -First 1)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Try = $i; Ms = $ms
            DC = $(if ($dc -match 'DC:\s*\\\\(\S+)') { $Matches[1] } else { 'NO ANSWER' })
            Address = $(if ($addr -match 'Address:\s*\\\\(\S+)') { $Matches[1] } else { '' })
            DcSite = $(if ($site -match 'Dc Site Name:\s*(\S+)') { $Matches[1] } else { '' })
            ClientSite = (($raw | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Our Site Name:\s*(\S+)' } | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match 'Our Site Name:\s*(\S+)') { $Matches[1] } }) | Select-Object -First 1)
        }
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
Asks DC Locator for a DC in a domain several times (forced, uncached) and reports which DCs it picked and how long each answer took.

If one DC shows up and it is slow or unhealthy (Get-DcHealthReport), that is the one logons hang on.

function Search-EventLogText {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Searches all event logs (System, Application, Security and every Applications and Services log) for text in the last hours.
.PARAMETER Text
Text or regular expression, e.g. AmsPlantServer|AmsServiceUser.
.PARAMETER Hours
How far back.
.PARAMETER MaxPerLog
Most events read per log.
.EXAMPLE
Search-EventLogText -Text 'AmsPlantServer|AmsServiceUser' -Hours 3
.NOTES
Takes a minute or two. Entries from Defender, AppLocker or CodeIntegrity point to a blocked program.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Text, [int]$Hours = 3, [int]$MaxPerLog = 2000)
    $start = (Get-Date).AddHours(-$Hours)
    foreach ($log in @(Get-WinEvent -ListLog * -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.RecordCount -gt 0 -and $_.LastWriteTime -ge $start })) {
        Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = $log.LogName; StartTime = $start } -MaxEvents $MaxPerLog -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $_.Message -match $Text } |
            Select-Object TimeCreated, LogName, ProviderName, Id, LevelDisplayName, @{ N = 'Message'; E = { ($_.Message -replace '\s+', ' ') } }
    }
}

function Get-FailedLogon {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Failed logons (event 4625) from the Security log, with the reason Windows gives.
.PARAMETER Hours
How far back to look.
.PARAMETER UserName
Only this account (wildcard allowed).
.PARAMETER Max
At most this many events.
.EXAMPLE
Get-FailedLogon -Hours 4 -UserName AmsServiceUser
.NOTES
Needs an elevated session. On a DC, lockout source details are in event 4740 instead.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [int]$Hours = 4,
        [string]$UserName = '*',
        [int]$Max = 200
    )
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'Security'; Id = 4625; StartTime = (Get-Date).AddHours(-$Hours) } -MaxEvents $Max -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        ForEach-Object {
            $x = [xml]$_.ToXml()
            $data = @{}
            foreach ($n in $x.Event.EventData.Data) { $data[$n.Name] = $n.'#text' }
            if ($data['TargetUserName'] -notlike $UserName) { return }
            [pscustomobject]@{
                Time        = $_.TimeCreated
                User        = "$($data['TargetDomainName'])\$($data['TargetUserName'])"
                LogonType   = $data['LogonType']
                Status      = $data['Status']
                SubStatus   = $data['SubStatus']
                Workstation = $data['WorkstationName']
                SourceIP    = $data['IpAddress']
                Process     = $data['ProcessName']
            }
        }
}

function Get-FolderAcl {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Who has which rights on a folder (like icacls), flagging entries that show only a SID (deleted or recreated accounts).
.PARAMETER Path
Folder or file.
.EXAMPLE
Get-FolderAcl -Path C:\AMS
.NOTES
A bare S-1-5-21-... entry means the account it belonged to no longer exists (or was recreated with a new SID).
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path)
    $acl = Get-Acl -LiteralPath $Path -ErrorAction Stop
    foreach ($a in $acl.Access) {
        $id = [string]$a.IdentityReference
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Path        = $Path
            Identity    = $id
            Rights      = [string]$a.FileSystemRights
            Type        = [string]$a.AccessControlType
            Inherited   = $a.IsInherited
            AppliesTo   = "$($a.InheritanceFlags)"
            OrphanedSid = ($id -match '^S-1-5-21-')
        }
    }
    [pscustomobject]@{ Path = $Path; Identity = "(owner) $($acl.Owner)"; Rights = ''; Type = ''; Inherited = $null; AppliesTo = ''; OrphanedSid = ([string]$acl.Owner -match '^S-1-5-21-') }
}
Entries.Notes:
Who has which rights on a folder (like icacls), flagging entries that show only a SID (deleted or recreated accounts).

A bare S-1-5-21-... entry means the account it belonged to no longer exists (or was recreated with a new SID).

function Backup-Folder {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Copies a folder to <Destination>\<FolderName>_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss> before you change something.
.PARAMETER Path
Folder to back up.
.PARAMETER Destination
Where to put the copy. Default: the folder's parent.
.EXAMPLE
Backup-Folder -Path C:\AMS\DB -Destination D:\Backups
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path,
        [string]$Destination
    )
    $src = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path -ErrorAction Stop).ProviderPath.TrimEnd('\')
    if (-not $Destination) { $Destination = Split-Path -Path $src -Parent }
    $target = Join-Path $Destination ("{0}_{1}" -f (Split-Path -Path $src -Leaf), (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'))
    if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($src, "Copy to $target")) {
        Copy-Item -LiteralPath $src -Destination $target -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Stop
        $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
        [pscustomobject]@{ Source = $src; Backup = $target; Files = $files.Count; MB = [math]::Round((($files | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum) / 1MB, 1) }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Copies a folder to <Destination>\<FolderName>_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss> before you change something.

function Grant-FolderPermission {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Grants NTFS rights on a folder (and everything under it) with icacls, then shows the resulting entries for that account.
.PARAMETER Path
Folder.
.PARAMETER Identity
Account, e.g. CONTOSO\svc-backup$ or CONTOSO\App-Users.
.PARAMETER Rights
R = read, RX = read and execute, M = modify, F = full control.
.PARAMETER ThisFolderOnly
Do not inherit to subfolders and files.
.EXAMPLE
Grant-FolderPermission -Path D:\Backups -Identity 'CONTOSO\svc-backup$' -Rights M
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path, [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Identity, [ValidateSet('R', 'RX', 'M', 'F')] [string]$Rights = 'M', [switch]$ThisFolderOnly)
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Container)) { throw "Folder not found: $Path" }
    $grant = if ($ThisFolderOnly) { "$($Identity):$Rights" } else { "$($Identity):(OI)(CI)$Rights" }
    if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($Path, "icacls /grant $grant")) {
        $out = @(icacls $Path /grant $grant 2>&1)
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "icacls failed: $($out -join ' ')" }
    }
    $short = ($Identity -split '\\')[-1]
    (Get-Acl -LiteralPath $Path).Access | Where-Object { [string]$_.IdentityReference -like "*$short" } |
        Select-Object @{ N = 'Path'; E = { $Path } }, IdentityReference, FileSystemRights, AccessControlType, IsInherited, InheritanceFlags
}
Entries.Notes: Grants NTFS rights on a folder (and everything under it) with icacls, then shows the resulting entries for that account.

Entries.Name: Log search
Entries.Description: Lines matching error/fail in a log.
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer with the log.
Entries.Code:
function Search-LogFile {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Lines in a log that match a pattern (default: error / fail / denied), with the lines around them.
.PARAMETER Path
Log file (wildcards allowed, e.g. C:\Windows\AMS*Install.log).
.PARAMETER Pattern
Regular expression. Default finds errors, failures and access denied.
.PARAMETER Context
Lines to show before and after each match.
.PARAMETER First
Only the first N matches (the first failure is usually the cause; later ones are fallout).
.PARAMETER Last
Only the last N matches.
.EXAMPLE
Search-LogFile -Path C:\Windows\AMSDeviceManager13_5Install.log -Pattern '\*\*\*ERROR\*\*\*' -First 25
.EXAMPLE
Search-LogFile -Path X:\Windows\Temp\SMSTS\smsts.log -Pattern 'fail' -First 1 -Context 10
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path,
        [string]$Pattern = 'error|fail|denied|exception',
        [int]$Context = 0,
        [int]$First = 0,
        [int]$Last = 0
    )
    $hits = @(Select-String -Path $Path -Pattern $Pattern -Context $Context, $Context -ErrorAction Stop)
    if ($First -gt 0) { $hits = @($hits | Select-Object -First $First) }
    if ($Last -gt 0) { $hits = @($hits | Select-Object -Last $Last) }
    foreach ($h in $hits) {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            File   = Split-Path -Path $h.Path -Leaf
            Line   = $h.LineNumber
            Text   = $h.Line.Trim()
            Before = ($h.Context.PreContext -join "`n")
            After  = ($h.Context.PostContext -join "`n")
        }
    }
}

function Get-GroupPolicyEvent {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Group Policy runs from the GroupPolicy/Operational log: start, finish and how long each took, plus slow-link detections and errors.
.PARAMETER Hours
How far back.
.PARAMETER Scope
Computer, User or both.
.EXAMPLE
Get-GroupPolicyEvent -Hours 4
.NOTES
If Group Policy itself only takes seconds, a slow logon is happening before it (DNS, Kerberos, DC discovery).
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([int]$Hours = 24, [ValidateSet('Both', 'Computer', 'User')] [string]$Scope = 'Both')
    $ids = 4000, 4001, 4016, 5016, 7016, 8000, 8001, 8004, 8005, 5312, 5314, 5320, 7320, 1129, 7017
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'Microsoft-Windows-GroupPolicy/Operational'; Id = $ids; StartTime = (Get-Date).AddHours(-$Hours) } -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $Scope -eq 'Both' -or ($Scope -eq 'Computer' -and $_.Id -in 4000, 8000, 8004 -or $_.Message -match 'computer') -or ($Scope -eq 'User' -and ($_.Id -in 4001, 8001, 8005 -or $_.Message -match 'user')) } |
        Sort-Object TimeCreated |
        Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, @{ N = 'What'; E = { switch ($_.Id) { 4000 { 'Computer GP start' } 4001 { 'User GP start' } 8000 { 'Computer GP finished' } 8001 { 'User GP finished' } 8004 { 'Computer GP finished (manual)' } 8005 { 'User GP finished (manual)' } 5312 { 'GPOs applied' } 5314 { 'Link speed / slow link' } 5320 { 'Info' } 4016 { 'Extension start' } 5016 { 'Extension finished' } 7016 { 'Extension failed' } 7320 { 'Error' } 1129 { 'No network / DC unreachable' } 7017 { 'Error' } default { '' } } } }, @{ N = 'Message'; E = { ($_.Message -replace '\s+', ' ') } }
}
Entries.Notes:
Group Policy runs from the GroupPolicy/Operational log: start, finish and how long each took, plus slow-link detections and errors.

If Group Policy itself only takes seconds, a slow logon is happening before it (DNS, Kerberos, DC discovery).

Entries.Name: GPMC installed?
Entries.Description: Are GPMC / RSAT GP tools here?
Entries.WhereToRun: Each server to check - use "Run on these computers" with names from Get-ADServerList.
Entries.Code:
function Get-GpmcStatus {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Whether the Group Policy Management tools (GPMC) are installed on this computer.
.DESCRIPTION
Checks the server feature (GPMC / RSAT-GPMC), the Windows 10/11 RSAT capability, and that
gpmc.msc exists. Run it on many servers with "Run on these computers".
.EXAMPLE
Get-GpmcStatus
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    $feature = ''
    if (Get-Command Get-WindowsFeature -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $feature = (@(Get-WindowsFeature -Name GPMC, RSAT-GPMC -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Installed) | ForEach-Object { $_.Name }) -join ', '
    }
    $cap = ''
    if (Get-Command Get-WindowsCapability -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $cap = (@(Get-WindowsCapability -Online -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -like '*GroupPolicy*' -and $_.State -eq 'Installed' }) | ForEach-Object { $_.Name }) -join ', '
    }
    $msc = Test-Path "$env:SystemRoot\System32\gpmc.msc"
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Computer        = $env:COMPUTERNAME
        GpmcInstalled   = ($msc -or [bool]$feature -or [bool]$cap)
        Feature         = $feature
        RsatCapability  = $cap
        GpmcMsc         = $msc
        OS              = (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
Whether the Group Policy Management tools (GPMC) are installed on this computer.
Checks the server feature (GPMC / RSAT-GPMC), the Windows 10/11 RSAT capability, and that
gpmc.msc exists. Run it on many servers with "Run on these computers".

function Export-GpResultReport {
<#
.SYNOPSIS

.PARAMETER Scope

    [pscustomobject]@{ Report = $Path; KB = [math]::Round((Get-Item $Path).Length / 1KB); Note = 'Open it in a browser. Component Status shows time per extension.' }

function Find-SysvolScriptText {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Searches the scripts in SYSVOL (ps1, vbs, bat, cmd) for a piece of text.
.PARAMETER Pattern
Text or regular expression to look for.
.PARAMETER Domain
Domain whose SYSVOL to search. Empty = current domain.
.EXAMPLE
Find-SysvolScriptText -Pattern 'wkstn_'
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Pattern,
        [string]$Domain
    )
    if (-not $Domain) { $Domain = $env:USERDNSDOMAIN }
    $root = "\\$Domain\SYSVOL\$Domain\Policies"
    Get-ChildItem -Path $root -Recurse -Include *.ps1, *.psm1, *.vbs, *.bat, *.cmd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |

Entries.Name: FlexLM ports
Entries.WhereToRun: The client PC that cannot get a license.
Entries.Code:
function Test-FlexLmPort {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Tests the lmgrd port range and an optional vendor daemon port on a license server.
.PARAMETER Server
License server.
.PARAMETER VendorPort
Vendor daemon port, if fixed in the license file.
.PARAMETER FirstPort
Start of the lmgrd range.
.PARAMETER LastPort
End of the lmgrd range.
.EXAMPLE
Test-FlexLmPort -Server lic01 -VendorPort 27010
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Server, [int]$VendorPort = 0, [int]$FirstPort = 27000, [int]$LastPort = 27009)
    $ports = @($FirstPort..$LastPort)
    if ($VendorPort -gt 0) { $ports += $VendorPort }
    foreach ($p in $ports) {
        $t = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient
        $ok = $false
        try { $iar = $t.BeginConnect($Server, $p, $null, $null); $ok = $iar.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne(1500) -and $t.Connected } catch { } finally { $t.Close() }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Server = $Server; Port = $p; Role = $(if ($p -eq $VendorPort) { 'Vendor daemon' } else { 'lmgrd range' }); Open = $ok }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Tests the lmgrd port range and an optional vendor daemon port on a license server.

function Get-TimeSkew {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Clock difference between this computer and other computers (Kerberos fails beyond 5 minutes).
.PARAMETER ComputerName
Computers to compare with, one per line (usually DCs of both domains).
.PARAMETER Samples
Samples per computer.
.EXAMPLE
Get-TimeSkew -ComputerName dc1.domain1.com, dc1.domain2.ads
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string[]]$ComputerName,
        [int]$Samples = 1
    )
    foreach ($c in $ComputerName) {
        $out = @(w32tm /stripchart /computer:$c /samples:$Samples /dataonly 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ })
        $offsets = @($out | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match ',\s*([+-]?\d+(\.\d+)?)s') { [double]$Matches[1] } })
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Computer      = $c
            OffsetSeconds = $(if ($offsets.Count) { [math]::Round(($offsets | Measure-Object -Average).Average, 3) } else { $null })
            Ok            = $(if ($offsets.Count) { [math]::Abs(($offsets | Measure-Object -Average).Average) -lt 300 } else { $false })
            Detail        = $(if ($offsets.Count) { '' } else { ($out | Where-Object { $_.Trim() } | Select-Object -Last 1) })
        }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Clock difference between this computer and other computers (Kerberos fails beyond 5 minutes).

Entries.Name: IPs per subnet
Entries.Description: Counts a list of IPs per /24.
Entries.WhereToRun: Anywhere - it works on the list you paste.

function Group-IpBySubnet {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Groups a pasted list of IP addresses by subnet (first three octets by default) and counts each.
.PARAMETER IPAddress
IP addresses, one per line (anything that is not an IPv4 address is skipped).
.PARAMETER PrefixLength
Group size: 24 = by first three octets, 16 = first two.
.EXAMPLE
Group-IpBySubnet -IPAddress 10.1.2.3, 10.1.2.40, 10.1.3.7
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string[]]$IPAddress, [ValidateSet(8, 16, 24)] [int]$PrefixLength = 24)
    $octets = $PrefixLength / 8
    $IPAddress | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$' } |
        Group-Object { (($_ -split '\.')[0..($octets - 1)] -join '.') + '.0/' + $PrefixLength } |
        Sort-Object Count -Descending |
        Select-Object @{ N = 'Subnet'; E = { $_.Name } }, Count, @{ N = 'Addresses'; E = { ($_.Group | Select-Object -First 20) -join ', ' } }
}
Entries.Notes: Groups a pasted list of IP addresses by subnet (first three octets by default) and counts each.

Entries.Name: Proxy settings
Entries.Description: WinHTTP and user proxy side by side.
Entries.WhereToRun: The computer with connection problems.
Entries.Code:
function Get-ProxySettings {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
The machine (WinHTTP) proxy that services and SYSTEM use, and the current user's browser proxy - they are often different.
.EXAMPLE
Get-ProxySettings
.NOTES
Machine-context calls (certificate enrollment, Windows Update, SCCM) use WinHTTP. Set it with "netsh winhttp set proxy" or "netsh winhttp import proxy source=ie".
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    $winhttp = (@(netsh winhttp show proxy 2>&1) | ForEach-Object { ([string]$_).Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch '^Current WinHTTP' }) -join ' | '
    $ie = Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $pol = Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [pscustomobject]@{
        WinHttp           = $winhttp
        UserProxyEnabled  = $(if ($ie) { [bool]$ie.ProxyEnable } else { $null })
        UserProxyServer   = $(if ($ie) { $ie.ProxyServer } else { '' })
        UserProxyBypass   = $(if ($ie) { $ie.ProxyOverride } else { '' })
        UserAutoConfigUrl = $(if ($ie) { $ie.AutoConfigURL } else { '' })
        PerMachinePolicy  = $(if ($pol) { [bool]$pol.ProxySettingsPerUser -eq $false } else { $false })
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
The machine (WinHTTP) proxy that services and SYSTEM use, and the current user's browser proxy - they are often different.

Machine-context calls (certificate enrollment, Windows Update, SCCM) use WinHTTP. Set it with "netsh winhttp set proxy" or "netsh winhttp import proxy source=ie".

function Get-ProcessDetail {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
How a program was launched and what it is talking to: full command line (the connect string), parent process, exe path and version, user, and its established TCP connections.
.PARAMETER Name
Process name (wildcards allowed), e.g. mstsc, javaw, AmsServerStarter.
.PARAMETER Id
Or a process id.
.EXAMPLE
Get-ProcessDetail -Name mstsc
.NOTES
Run elevated to see processes of other users.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Name = '*', [int]$Id = 0)
    $filter = if ($Id -gt 0) { "ProcessId = $Id" } else { "Name LIKE '" + ($Name -replace '\*', '%' -replace "'", "''") + $(if ($Name -notmatch '\.exe$' -and $Name -notmatch '\*$') { ".exe'" } else { "'" }) }
    $procs = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter $filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    $conns = @(Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    foreach ($p in $procs) {
        $parent = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId = $($p.ParentProcessId)" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $owner = ''
        try { $o = Invoke-CimMethod -InputObject $p -MethodName GetOwner -ErrorAction Stop; if ($o.User) { $owner = "$($o.Domain)\$($o.User)" } } catch { }
        $ver = ''
        if ($p.ExecutablePath) { try { $ver = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $p.ExecutablePath -ErrorAction Stop).VersionInfo.FileVersion } catch { } }
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Name        = $p.Name
            PID         = $p.ProcessId
            User        = $owner
            CommandLine = $p.CommandLine
            Path        = $p.ExecutablePath
            Version     = $ver
            Parent      = $(if ($parent) { "$($parent.Name) ($($parent.ProcessId))" } else { "($($p.ParentProcessId) - exited)" })
            Started     = $p.CreationDate
            Connections = ((@($conns | Where-Object { $_.OwningProcess -eq $p.ProcessId }) | ForEach-Object { "$($_.RemoteAddress):$($_.RemotePort)" }) -join '; ')
        }
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
How a program was launched and what it is talking to: full command line (the connect string), parent process, exe path and version, user, and its established TCP connections.

Run elevated to see processes of other users.

function Get-ServiceFailureEvent {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Service Control Manager events for a service: failed to start (7000/7001/7009/7011), terminated with error (7023/7024), crashed (7031/7034).
.PARAMETER Name
Service name or display name text, e.g. WDSServer. Empty = all services.
.PARAMETER Days
How far back to look.
.EXAMPLE
Get-ServiceFailureEvent -Name WDSServer -Days 30
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Name, [int]$Days = 7)
    $ids = 7000, 7001, 7009, 7011, 7022, 7023, 7024, 7031, 7034, 7043
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'System'; ProviderName = 'Service Control Manager'; Id = $ids; StartTime = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$Days) } -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { -not $Name -or $_.Message -like "*$Name*" } |
        Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, @{ N = 'Meaning'; E = { switch ($_.Id) { 7000 { 'failed to start' } 7001 { 'dependency failed' } 7009 { 'start timed out' } 7011 { 'response timed out' } 7022 { 'hung on start' } 7023 { 'terminated with error' } 7024 { 'terminated with service error' } 7031 { 'crashed (recovery taken)' } 7034 { 'crashed unexpectedly' } 7043 { 'did not shut down' } } } }, @{ N = 'Message'; E = { $_.Message -replace '\s+', ' ' } }
}
Entries.Notes: Service Control Manager events for a service: failed to start (7000/7001/7009/7011), terminated with error (7023/7024), crashed (7031/7034).

Entries.Name: Service recovery

function Set-ServiceRecovery {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Sets a service's Recovery options to restart it after the first, second and later failures (sc.exe failure).
.PARAMETER Name
Service name.
.PARAMETER RestartDelaySeconds
Wait before each restart.
.PARAMETER ResetAfterDays
Reset the failure count after this many days without a failure.
.PARAMETER DelayedStart
Also set the start type to Automatic (Delayed Start) - helps services that fail at boot.
.EXAMPLE
Set-ServiceRecovery -Name WDSServer -DelayedStart
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Name,
        [int]$RestartDelaySeconds = 60,
        [int]$ResetAfterDays = 1,
        [switch]$DelayedStart
    )
    if (-not (Get-Service -Name $Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw "Service not found: $Name" }
    $ms = $RestartDelaySeconds * 1000
    if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($Name, "Restart on failure after $RestartDelaySeconds s")) {
        $out = sc.exe failure $Name reset= ($ResetAfterDays * 86400) actions= "restart/$ms/restart/$ms/restart/$ms" 2>&1
        if ($DelayedStart) { $out2 = sc.exe config $Name start= delayed-auto 2>&1; $out = "$out | $out2" }
        $q = (sc.exe qfailure $Name 2>&1) -join "`n"
        [pscustomobject]@{ Service = $Name; Result = ([string]$out).Trim(); Current = $q }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Sets a service's Recovery options to restart it after the first, second and later failures (sc.exe failure).

function Find-LogFailure {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Finds the first (or every) line matching failure words in a log and shows the lines before and after it - the first failure is usually the real cause.
.PARAMETER Path
Log file.
.PARAMETER Pattern
Words to look for (regular expression).
.PARAMETER Context
Lines before and after.
.PARAMETER All
Every match, not just the first.
.EXAMPLE
Find-LogFailure -Path C:\Windows\CCM\Logs\SMSTSLog\smsts.log
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Path, [string]$Pattern = 'fail|error|0x8[0-9a-f]{7}|denied|cannot|unable', [int]$Context = 5, [switch]$All)
    $hits = @(Select-String -LiteralPath $Path -Pattern $Pattern -Context $Context, $Context -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.Line -notmatch 'error\s*=\s*0\b|Failed\s*=\s*0|0x00000000' })
    if (-not $All) { $hits = @($hits | Select-Object -First 1) }
    foreach ($h in $hits) {
        $text = @()
        $n = $h.LineNumber - $h.Context.PreContext.Count
        foreach ($l in $h.Context.PreContext) { $text += ('{0,6}   {1}' -f $n, ($l -replace '<!\[LOG\[|\]LOG\]!>.*$', '')); $n++ }
        $text += ('{0,6} > {1}' -f $h.LineNumber, ($h.Line -replace '<!\[LOG\[|\]LOG\]!>.*$', '')); $n++
        foreach ($l in $h.Context.PostContext) { $text += ('{0,6}   {1}' -f $n, ($l -replace '<!\[LOG\[|\]LOG\]!>.*$', '')); $n++ }
        $text -join "`n"
        ''
    }
    if (-not $hits.Count) { "No lines match '$Pattern' in $Path" }
}
Entries.Notes: Finds the first (or every) line matching failure words in a log and shows the lines before and after it - the first failure is usually the real cause.

function Get-SccmClientInfo {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Configuration Manager client version, assigned site, current management point, cache size and location, and the CcmExec service state.
.EXAMPLE
Get-SccmClientInfo
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    $svc = Get-Service -Name CcmExec -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $svc) { return [pscustomobject]@{ Computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Client = 'Not installed (no CcmExec service)' } }
    $c = Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Client -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $a = Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Authority -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
    $cache = Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm\SoftMgmtAgent -ClassName CacheConfig -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME; Service = [string]$svc.Status; Version = $(if ($c) { $c.ClientVersion } else { '' })
        Site = $(if ($a) { $a.Name -replace '^SMS:' } else { '' }); ManagementPoint = $(if ($a) { $a.CurrentManagementPoint } else { '' })
        CacheMB = $(if ($cache) { $cache.Size } else { $null }); CachePath = $(if ($cache) { $cache.Location } else { '' })
        LogFolder = "$env:windir\CCM\Logs"
    }
}

function Find-SccmLog {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Finds the Configuration Manager logs wherever they are on this computer (client, server, PXE DP, task sequence and WinPE locations), newest first.
.PARAMETER Name
Log name pattern, e.g. smsts*, SMSPXE*, AppEnforce*. Default = all .log files in those folders.
.EXAMPLE
Find-SccmLog -Name smsts*
.NOTES
In WinPE the task sequence log is X:\Windows\Temp\SMSTSLog\smsts.log (or C:\_SMSTaskSequence\Logs once the disk is formatted).
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Name = '*.log')
    if ($Name -notmatch '\.') { $Name = "$Name.log" }
    $folders = @("$env:windir\CCM\Logs", "$env:windir\CCM\Logs\SMSTSLog", "$env:windir\Temp\SMSTSLog", 'C:\_SMSTaskSequence\Logs', 'X:\Windows\Temp\SMSTSLog', 'X:\SMSTSLog', "$env:ProgramFiles\SMS_CCM\Logs", "$env:ProgramFiles\Microsoft Configuration Manager\Logs", "$env:windir\System32\SMSPXE", 'C:\SMS_DP$\sms\logs', "$env:windir\SMSTSLog")
    foreach ($d in (Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.Root })) { $folders += (Join-Path $d 'SMS_DP$\sms\logs'); $folders += (Join-Path $d 'Program Files\SMS_CCM\Logs') }
    $folders | Select-Object -Unique | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } |
        ForEach-Object { Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_ -Filter $Name -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } |
        Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
        Select-Object Name, LastWriteTime, @{ N = 'KB'; E = { [math]::Round($_.Length / 1KB) } }, FullName
}
Entries.Notes:
Finds the Configuration Manager logs wherever they are on this computer (client, server, PXE DP, task sequence and WinPE locations), newest first.

In WinPE the task sequence log is X:\Windows\Temp\SMSTSLog\smsts.log (or C:\_SMSTaskSequence\Logs once the disk is formatted).

Entries.Name: SCCM MP check

function Register-ScheduledScriptTask {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Creates a daily scheduled task that runs a script as a service account or gMSA, whether or not anyone is logged on.
.DESCRIPTION
For a gMSA, give the account name ending in $ and leave Credential empty (no password is
stored). For a regular service account, give Credential. The account needs "Log on as a
batch job" on this server, Read on the script folder and Modify on its log folder.
.PARAMETER TaskName
Name of the task.
.PARAMETER ScriptPath
Full path of the script the task runs.
.PARAMETER At
Time of day, e.g. 10:00 or 6:00am.
.PARAMETER Account
gMSA as DOMAIN\name$ (leave Credential empty).
.PARAMETER Credential
A regular service account (DOMAIN\svc-name and its password). Leave empty for a gMSA.
.PARAMETER RunHighest
Run with highest privileges (only if the script needs admin).
.EXAMPLE
Register-ScheduledScriptTask -TaskName 'Password Expiry Notice' -ScriptPath C:\Scripts\PwdNotify\PasswordExpiry.ps1 -At 6:00am -Account 'CONTOSO\svc-PwdNotify$'
.NOTES
A gMSA cannot be picked in the Task Scheduler GUI; edit such a task later with Set-ScheduledTask.
Test with: right-click the task > Run, then check Last Run Result (0x0 = success).
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$TaskName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$ScriptPath,
        [string]$At = '10:00',
        [string]$Account,
        [pscredential]$Credential,
        [switch]$RunHighest
    )
    if (-not $Account -and -not $Credential) { throw 'Give -Account (a gMSA ending in $) or -Credential (a service account).' }
    $dir = Split-Path -Path $ScriptPath -Parent
    $action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File `"$ScriptPath`"" -WorkingDirectory $dir
    $trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At ([datetime]$At)
    $settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable -ExecutionTimeLimit (New-TimeSpan -Hours 1)
    $level = if ($RunHighest) { 'Highest' } else { 'Limited' }
    if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($TaskName, "Register daily task at $At running $ScriptPath")) { return }
    if ($Credential) {
        $t = Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings -User $Credential.UserName -Password $Credential.GetNetworkCredential().Password -RunLevel $level
    }
    else {
        $principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId $Account -LogonType Password -RunLevel $level
        $t = Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings -Principal $principal
    }
    $t | Select-Object TaskName, State, @{ N = 'RunAs'; E = { $_.Principal.UserId } }, @{ N = 'Next'; E = { (Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $TaskName).NextRunTime } }
}
Entries.Notes:
Creates a daily scheduled task that runs a script as a service account or gMSA, whether or not anyone is logged on.
For a gMSA, give the account name ending in $ and leave Credential empty (no password is
stored). For a regular service account, give Credential. The account needs "Log on as a
batch job" on this server, Read on the script folder and Modify on its log folder.

A gMSA cannot be picked in the Task Scheduler GUI; edit such a task later with Set-ScheduledTask.
Test with: right-click the task > Run, then check Last Run Result (0x0 = success).

function Install-ChromeOffline {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Closes Chrome, installs the enterprise MSI with a log, turns off Google Update, copies initial_preferences and removes the public desktop shortcut.
.PARAMETER MsiPath
GoogleChromeStandaloneEnterprise64.msi.
.PARAMETER InitialPreferences
Optional initial_preferences file to copy next to chrome.exe.
.PARAMETER KeepDesktopShortcut
Leave the Public Desktop shortcut.
.EXAMPLE
Install-ChromeOffline -MsiPath \\server\pkg\GoogleChromeStandaloneEnterprise64.msi -InitialPreferences \\server\pkg\initial_preferences
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$MsiPath, [string]$InitialPreferences, [switch]$KeepDesktopShortcut)
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $MsiPath)) { throw "Not found: $MsiPath" }
    if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($env:COMPUTERNAME, "Install Chrome from $MsiPath")) { return }
    Get-Process chrome -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    $log = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'ChromeInstall.log'
    $p = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i `"$MsiPath`" /qn /norestart /l*v `"$log`"" -Wait -PassThru
    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Update'
    New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name UpdateDefault -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name AutoUpdateCheckPeriodMinutes -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force | Out-Null
    $chromeDir = @("${env:ProgramFiles}\Google\Chrome\Application", "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Google\Chrome\Application") | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $_ 'chrome.exe')) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($InitialPreferences -and $chromeDir) { Copy-Item -LiteralPath $InitialPreferences -Destination (Join-Path $chromeDir 'initial_preferences') -Force }
    if (-not $KeepDesktopShortcut) { Remove-Item "$env:PUBLIC\Desktop\Google Chrome.lnk" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
    [pscustomobject]@{ Computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME; ExitCode = $p.ExitCode; Version = $(if ($chromeDir) { (Get-Item (Join-Path $chromeDir 'chrome.exe')).VersionInfo.ProductVersion } else { '(chrome.exe not found)' }); Log = $log; InitialPreferences = [bool]($InitialPreferences -and $chromeDir) }
}
Entries.Notes: Closes Chrome, installs the enterprise MSI with a log, turns off Google Update, copies initial_preferences and removes the public desktop shortcut.

function Uninstall-UserChrome {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Removes Chrome installed under a user's AppData using its own setup.exe (--uninstall --force-uninstall), then cleans the leftover folder.
.PARAMETER UserName
Profile folder name under C:\Users. Empty = the current user.
.EXAMPLE
Uninstall-UserChrome -UserName jsmith
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param([string]$UserName = $env:USERNAME)
    $base = "C:\Users\$UserName\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\Application"
    if (-not (Test-Path $base)) { return [pscustomobject]@{ User = $UserName; Result = 'No per-user Chrome' } }
    $setup = Get-ChildItem -Path $base -Filter setup.exe -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess("$UserName ($base)", 'Uninstall per-user Chrome')) { return }
    Get-Process chrome -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Path -like "$base*" } | Stop-Process -Force
    $code = $null
    if ($setup) { $code = (Start-Process -FilePath $setup.FullName -ArgumentList '--uninstall --force-uninstall' -Wait -PassThru).ExitCode }
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $base -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [pscustomobject]@{ User = $UserName; SetupExitCode = $code; Remaining = (Test-Path $base); Result = $(if (Test-Path $base) { 'Folder still there (in use?)' } else { 'Removed' }) }
}
Entries.Notes: Removes Chrome installed under a user's AppData using its own setup.exe (--uninstall --force-uninstall), then cleans the leftover folder.

function Get-InstalledSoftware {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Installed programs from the uninstall registry keys (64-bit, 32-bit and loaded user hives).
.PARAMETER Name
Wildcard on the display name, e.g. *Firefox* or *AMS*.
.EXAMPLE
Get-InstalledSoftware -Name '*Firefox*'
.NOTES
Per-user installs only show for users whose profile is loaded (logged on). Store apps are
not listed - see Find-FirefoxInstall for an example that checks Appx too.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Name = '*')
    $paths = @(
        'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*',
        'HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*',
        'Registry::HKEY_USERS\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*'
    )
    Get-ItemProperty -Path $paths -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -and $_.DisplayName -like $Name } |
        ForEach-Object {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                Computer        = $env:COMPUTERNAME
                DisplayName     = $_.DisplayName
                Version         = $_.DisplayVersion
                Publisher       = $_.Publisher
                InstallLocation = $_.InstallLocation
                Scope           = $(if ($_.PSPath -like '*HKEY_USERS*') { 'User' } elseif ($_.PSPath -like '*WOW6432Node*') { 'Machine (32-bit)' } else { 'Machine' })
                MSI             = ($_.WindowsInstaller -eq 1)
                UninstallKey    = $_.PSChildName
            }
        } | Sort-Object DisplayName
}
Entries.Notes:
Installed programs from the uninstall registry keys (64-bit, 32-bit and loaded user hives).

Per-user installs only show for users whose profile is loaded (logged on). Store apps are
not listed - see Find-FirefoxInstall for an example that checks Appx too.

function Get-AppCrashEvent {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Application crash events: faulting program, module, exception code (1000), and .NET unhandled exceptions with the stack (1026).
.PARAMETER Program
Text in the program name, e.g. RA.FTAC.Server. Empty = all.
.PARAMETER Days
How far back.
.EXAMPLE
Get-AppCrashEvent -Program RA.FTAC.Server -Days 14
.NOTES
Exception codes: 0xc0000005 access violation, 0xc0000409 stack buffer overrun, 0xc00001a5 invalid exception handler, 0xe0434352 .NET exception (see the 1026 event).
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Program, [int]$Days = 7)
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'Application'; Id = 1000, 1026, 1002; StartTime = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$Days) } -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { -not $Program -or $_.Message -like "*$Program*" } |
        ForEach-Object {
            $m = $_.Message
            [pscustomobject]@{
                Time      = $_.TimeCreated
                Id        = $_.Id
                Kind      = switch ($_.Id) { 1000 { 'Crash' } 1026 { '.NET unhandled exception' } 1002 { 'Hang' } }
                Program   = $(if ($m -match 'Faulting application name: ([^,\r\n]+)') { $Matches[1] } elseif ($m -match 'Application: ([^\r\n]+)') { $Matches[1] } else { '' })
                Module    = $(if ($m -match 'Faulting module name: ([^,\r\n]+)') { $Matches[1] } else { '' })
                Exception = $(if ($m -match 'Exception code: (\S+)') { $Matches[1] } elseif ($m -match 'Exception Info: ([^\r\n]+)') { $Matches[1] } else { '' })
                Detail    = (($m -split "`r?`n" | Select-Object -First 6) -join ' ').Trim()
            }
        }
}
Entries.Notes:
Application crash events: faulting program, module, exception code (1000), and .NET unhandled exceptions with the stack (1026).

Exception codes: 0xc0000005 access violation, 0xc0000409 stack buffer overrun, 0xc00001a5 invalid exception handler, 0xe0434352 .NET exception (see the 1026 event).

function Enable-WerLocalDump {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Turns on Windows Error Reporting LocalDumps for one program, so its next crash leaves a full dump for the vendor or WinDbg.
.PARAMETER ExeName
Program file name, e.g. RA.FTAC.Server.exe.
.PARAMETER DumpFolder
Where dumps are written.
.PARAMETER Count
How many dumps to keep.
.PARAMETER Disable
Remove the setting for this program instead.
.EXAMPLE
Enable-WerLocalDump -ExeName RA.FTAC.Server.exe
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$ExeName, [string]$DumpFolder = 'C:\CrashDumps', [int]$Count = 3, [switch]$Disable)
    $key = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\LocalDumps\$ExeName"
    if ($Disable) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ExeName, 'Remove LocalDumps')) { Remove-Item -Path $key -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; [pscustomobject]@{ Program = $ExeName; LocalDumps = 'Removed' } }
        return
    }
    if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ExeName, "Full dumps to $DumpFolder")) {
        New-Item -Path $DumpFolder -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null
        New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
        New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name DumpFolder -PropertyType ExpandString -Value $DumpFolder -Force | Out-Null
        New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name DumpCount -PropertyType DWord -Value $Count -Force | Out-Null
        New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name DumpType -PropertyType DWord -Value 2 -Force | Out-Null
        [pscustomobject]@{ Program = $ExeName; LocalDumps = 'Full dumps on'; Folder = $DumpFolder; Keep = $Count }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Turns on Windows Error Reporting LocalDumps for one program, so its next crash leaves a full dump for the vendor or WinDbg.

function Find-CrashDump {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Crash dump files (.dmp) and Windows Error Reporting folders, newest first.
.PARAMETER Program
Text in the dump or report name. Empty = all.
.PARAMETER Days
Only files from the last N days.
.EXAMPLE
Find-CrashDump -Program RA.FTAC
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$Program, [int]$Days = 30)
    $since = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$Days)
    $places = @("$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive", "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportQueue", "$env:SystemRoot\Minidump", "$env:SystemRoot\MEMORY.DMP", "$env:ProgramData\CrashDumps")
    $places += @(Get-ChildItem "$env:SystemDrive\Users\*\AppData\Local\CrashDumps" -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName })
    foreach ($pl in $places) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pl)) { continue }
        Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $pl -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $_.LastWriteTime -ge $since -and ($_.Extension -eq '.dmp' -or $_.Name -eq 'Report.wer' -or $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Parent.Name -match 'Report(Archive|Queue)') } |
            Where-Object { -not $Program -or $_.FullName -like "*$Program*" } |
            Select-Object @{ N = 'Type'; E = { if ($_.Extension -eq '.dmp') { 'Dump' } elseif ($_.PSIsContainer) { 'WER report folder' } else { 'WER report' } } }, FullName, LastWriteTime, @{ N = 'MB'; E = { if ($_.PSIsContainer) { $null } else { [math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 1) } } }
    }
}
Entries.Notes: Crash dump files (.dmp) and Windows Error Reporting folders, newest first.

function Find-RecentLogFile {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
The newest .log files under one or more folders (find the log of a failed install).
.PARAMETER Path
Folders to search, one per line. Default: the temp folder.
.PARAMETER Count
How many files to list.
.PARAMETER Tail
Also show the last lines of the newest file.
.EXAMPLE
Find-RecentLogFile -Path $env:TEMP, C:\AMS -Count 10
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [string[]]$Path = @($env:TEMP),
        [int]$Count = 10,
        [int]$Tail = 0

    $files = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $Path -Recurse -Filter *.log -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First $Count)
    $files | Select-Object FullName, LastWriteTime, @{ N = 'KB'; E = { [math]::Round($_.Length / 1KB, 1) } }

        Write-Host "`n--- last $Tail lines of $($files[0].FullName) ---"
        Get-Content -LiteralPath $files[0].FullName -Tail $Tail | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }

function Set-LocalUserPassword {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Sets a new password on a local account, optionally so it never expires, and enables it.

        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Name,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [securestring]$Password,

    }
}

The session you are in: computer, user, domain, logon server, session type (Console / RDP / Citrix ICA) and the client device you connected from.
.EXAMPLE
Get-SessionContext
.NOTES
Useful when writing an SOP: over RDP or Citrix the physical box is not the story - the session host is.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    $sess = [string]$env:SESSIONNAME
    $type = if ($sess -like 'RDP-Tcp*') { 'Remote Desktop' } elseif ($sess -like 'ICA*') { 'Citrix ICA' } elseif ($sess -eq 'Console') { 'Console' } elseif (-not $sess) { 'Service / non-interactive' } else { $sess }
    $os = Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Computer     = $env:COMPUTERNAME
        User         = "$env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME"
        UserDnsDomain = $env:USERDNSDOMAIN
        LogonServer  = ([string]$env:LOGONSERVER).TrimStart('\')
        SessionName  = $sess
        SessionType  = $type
        ClientName   = $env:CLIENTNAME
        IPAddresses  = ((@(Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notlike '127.*' -and $_.IPAddress -notlike '169.254*' }) | ForEach-Object { $_.IPAddress }) -join ', ')
        OS           = $(if ($os) { $os.Caption } else { '' })
        LastBoot     = $(if ($os) { $os.LastBootUpTime } else { $null })
        Elevated     = ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
The session you are in: computer, user, domain, logon server, session type (Console / RDP / Citrix ICA) and the client device you connected from.

Useful when writing an SOP: over RDP or Citrix the physical box is not the story - the session host is.

Entries.Description: Display memory for a monitor layout.
Entries.WhereToRun: Anywhere - it is a calculation.
Entries.Code:
function Get-CitrixDisplayMemoryEstimate {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Estimates the display memory (KB) a Citrix session needs for a set of monitors, to compare with the "Display memory limit" policy.
.PARAMETER Resolution
One per monitor, as WIDTHxHEIGHT, e.g. 1920x1080.
.PARAMETER ColorDepth
Bits per pixel.
.EXAMPLE
Get-CitrixDisplayMemoryEstimate -Resolution 1920x1080, 1920x1080, 2560x1440
.NOTES
Estimate only: width x height x bytes per pixel, summed over monitors (the bounding rectangle is used when monitors are different heights). If the session falls back to fewer monitors or lower colour, raise the policy above this.
#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string[]]$Resolution, [ValidateSet(16, 24, 32)] [int]$ColorDepth = 32)
    $w = 0; $h = 0; $sum = 0
    foreach ($r in $Resolution) {
        if ($r -notmatch '^\s*(\d+)\s*[xX*]\s*(\d+)\s*$') { throw "Not WIDTHxHEIGHT: $r" }
        $w += [int]$Matches[1]; $h = [math]::Max($h, [int]$Matches[2]); $sum += [int]$Matches[1] * [int]$Matches[2]
    }
    $bpp = $ColorDepth / 8
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Monitors = $Resolution.Count; Layout = "${w}x$h"; ColorDepth = $ColorDepth
        SumKB = [math]::Ceiling($sum * $bpp / 1KB); BoundingBoxKB = [math]::Ceiling($w * $h * $bpp / 1KB)
        Suggested = "Set Display memory limit >= $([math]::Ceiling($w * $h * $bpp / 1KB)) KB"
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
Estimates the display memory (KB) a Citrix session needs for a set of monitors, to compare with the "Display memory limit" policy.

Estimate only: width x height x bytes per pixel, summed over monitors (the bounding rectangle is used when monitors are different heights). If the session falls back to fewer monitors or lower colour, raise the policy above this.
