    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([ValidateRange(2, 8)] [int]$Words = 3, [ValidateRange(1, 100)] [int]$Count = 5, [string]$Separator = '-')
    $list = @('Adventure', 'Afternoon', 'Allowance', 'Ambassador', 'Anchorage', 'Apartment', 'Architect', 'Assistant', 'Astronaut', 'Atmosphere', 'Avalanche', 'Background', 'Basketball', 'Blueberry', 'Bookshelf', 'Boulevard', 'Breakfast', 'Brilliance', 'Butterfly', 'Calculator', 'Calendar', 'Candlelight', 'Carpenter', 'Cathedral', 'Celebrate', 'Champion', 'Chocolate', 'Classroom', 'Clockwork', 'Collector', 'Community', 'Compassion', 'Composer', 'Confidence', 'Constant', 'Courtyard', 'Craftsman', 'Crossroads', 'Curiosity', 'Dandelion', 'Daylight', 'Delegate', 'Destination', 'Diamond', 'Discovery', 'Dragonfly', 'Education', 'Elevation', 'Embassy', 'Encounter', 'Endeavor', 'Equation', 'Evergreen', 'Excellent', 'Expedition', 'Fireplace', 'Fireworks', 'Flagship', 'Footprint', 'Headlight', 'Heritage', 'Highland', 'Horizon', 'Hurricane', 'Illustrate', 'Important', 'Ingredient', 'Innovator', 'Inspector', 'Instrument', 'Integrity', 'Invention', 'Jellyfish', 'Journalist', 'Kilometer', 'Kingfisher', 'Landscape', 'Lavender', 'Lighthouse', 'Limestone', 'Lionheart', 'Magnolia', 'Mainframe', 'Marathon', 'Marigold', 'Meadowlark', 'Mechanic', 'Membrane', 'Milestone', 'Moonlight', 'Mountain', 'Narrative', 'Navigator', 'Nightfall', 'Notebook', 'Objective', 'Observatory', 'Operator', 'Orchestra', 'Overnight', 'Paintbrush', 'Paragraph', 'Passenger', 'Pathfinder', 'Peppermint', 'Performer', 'Pineapple', 'Pinnacle', 'Platinum', 'Playground', 'Porcupine', 'Principal', 'Professor', 'Quarterly', 'Raincoat', 'Raspberry', 'Reference', 'Reflection', 'Riverbank', 'Sandstone', 'Satellite', 'Scientist', 'Seashore', 'Sentinel', 'Signature', 'Skylight', 'Snowflake', 'Something', 'Spectrum', 'Starlight', 'Strategic', 'Strawberry', 'Submarine', 'Sunflower',     $sym = '!@#$%&*?'

Entries.Name: Wake-on-LAN
Entries.WhereToRun: A computer on the same subnet as the targets (or a router that forwards directed broadcasts).
Entries.Code:
function Send-WakeOnLan {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Sends a Wake-on-LAN magic packet to wake computers that are off.
.DESCRIPTION
A magic packet is 6 x 0xFF then the MAC address 16 times, sent by UDP broadcast. Use the
subnet-directed broadcast (e.g. 192.168.1.255): 255.255.255.255 often does not leave the
local segment. To wake across subnets/VLANs, the router must forward directed broadcasts,
or run this on a computer in the target subnet ("Run on these computers").
.PARAMETER MacAddress
MAC addresses, one per line (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, AA-BB-... or AABBCC...).
.PARAMETER BroadcastIP
Broadcast address of the target subnet.
.PARAMETER Port
UDP port, 9 (or 7).
.EXAMPLE
Send-WakeOnLan -MacAddress 'AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF' -BroadcastIP 192.168.1.255
.NOTES
The target NIC and BIOS must have Wake-on-LAN enabled, and "fast startup" can stop it on Windows 10/11.
#>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string[]]$MacAddress,
        [string]$BroadcastIP = '255.255.255.255',
        [ValidateSet(7, 9)] [int]$Port = 9
    )
    foreach ($m in $MacAddress) {
        $mac = $m -replace '[:\-\.\s]', ''
        if ($mac -notmatch '^[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}$') { Write-Error "Invalid MAC address: $m"; continue }
        $macBytes = for ($i = 0; $i -lt 12; $i += 2) { [Convert]::ToByte($mac.Substring($i, 2), 16) }
        $packet = [byte[]](@(0xFF) * 6 + (@($macBytes) * 16))
        if (-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess("$m via $BroadcastIP`:$Port", 'Send magic packet')) { continue }
        $udp = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.UdpClient
        try {
            $udp.EnableBroadcast = $true
            [void]$udp.Send($packet, $packet.Length, $BroadcastIP, $Port)
            [pscustomobject]@{ MacAddress = $m; BroadcastIP = $BroadcastIP; Port = $Port; Sent = $true; Bytes = $packet.Length }
        }
        finally { $udp.Close() }
    }
}
Entries.Notes:
Sends a Wake-on-LAN magic packet to wake computers that are off.
A magic packet is 6 x 0xFF then the MAC address 16 times, sent by UDP broadcast. Use the
subnet-directed broadcast (e.g. 192.168.1.255): 255.255.255.255 often does not leave the
local segment. To wake across subnets/VLANs, the router must forward directed broadcasts,
or run this on a computer in the target subnet ("Run on these computers").

The target NIC and BIOS must have Wake-on-LAN enabled, and "fast startup" can stop it on Windows 10/11.

function Search-CbsLog {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Error lines from CBS.log (Windows servicing) - why an update, feature install or DISM repair failed.
.PARAMETER Pattern
Text to look for. Default: errors and failures.
.PARAMETER Last
Only the last N matches.

Search-CbsLog -Pattern 'HydrateFile|LxssManager' -Last 30

}
